equation_request.abstract: The quantum Fourier transform (QFT) is a key ingredient of several quantum algorithms and a qudit-specific implementation of the QFT is hence an important step toward the realization of qudit-based quantum computers. This work develops a circuit decomposition of the QFT for hybrid qudits based on generalized Hadamard and generalized controlled-phase gates, which can be implemented using selective rotations in NMR. We experimentally implement the hybrid qudit QFT on an NMR quantum emulator, which uses four qubits to emulate a single qutrit coupled to two qubits.

specification.problem: Develop a circuit decomposition of the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) for hybrid qudits (e.g., a qutrit plus qubits) using generalized Hadamard and generalized controlled-phase gates, implementable via selective rotations in NMR, and demonstrate it on an NMR quantum emulator in which four qubits emulate a qutrit coupled to two qubits.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the hybrid-qudit QFT: the standard QFT definition, the generalized Hadamard and controlled-phase gate forms as background, and a finite qutrit+2 qubit instance. The exact decomposition, pulse sequences, and experimental results are not given in the abstract.

symbols.meaning: Dimension of the qudit or hybrid system level
d-th root of unity e^{2\pi i/d}
Generalized controlled-phase gate between levels of dimension d and d'

equations.label: QFT definition
equations.description: Standard QFT action on a basis state, with N the total dimension (e.g., 3*2*2=12 for the hybrid instance).
equations.justification: Textbook definition of the QFT; the abstract names the QFT but gives no formula.
assumptions: N equals the product of the subsystem dimensions

equations.label: Generalized Hadamard
equations.description: Assumed form of the generalized Hadamard as the d-dimensional DFT matrix.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions generalized Hadamard gates without a definition; the DFT form is the common convention.
assumptions: Paper's generalized Hadamard matches the DFT matrix

equations.label: Generalized controlled-phase
equations.description: Assumed diagonal phase gate coupling levels of subsystems of dimension d and d'.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions generalized controlled-phase gates; this is the standard mixed-radix form and may differ from the paper.
assumptions: Phase convention follows mixed-radix QFT decomposition

registers.name: q
registers.role: Qutrit subsystem, most significant digit; the emulator encodes its 3 levels in a 4-level two-qubit space

registers.name: a
registers.role: First qubit coupled to the qutrit

registers.name: b
registers.role: Second qubit coupled to the qutrit

specification.initial_state: Assumed: a computational basis state |j_q, j_a, j_b> (or a thermal-equilibrium-derived pseudo-pure state in NMR); the abstract does not specify the input.

steps.description: Apply generalized Hadamard H_3 on the qutrit (implemented via selective rotations on the emulating qubits).
Apply generalized controlled-phase gates between the qutrit and each qubit, with mixed-radix phases.
Apply Hadamard H_2 on the first qubit, then controlled-phase between the two qubits.
Apply Hadamard H_2 on the last qubit; reverse digit order (swap) if required by the mixed-radix convention. Overall action is the QFT on dimension 12.

specification.measurement: Assumed: read out the NMR spectra (ensemble signal) of the emulating qubits after the QFT circuit, possibly via state tomography, to compare with the ideal QFT output; the abstract does not specify the protocol.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: compare the experimental output (spectra or reconstructed density matrix) with the ideal F_12 output, e.g., via a fidelity measure; the abstract gives no details.
